summary: The retrieval_benchmark required check does not reject lexical channel substitution. Feeding the acceptance gate a ranking produced entirely by the single SQLite FTS5 index, where every candidate carries LEXICAL provenance, the gate accepts all eleven lanes at recall 1.00 and nDCG 1.00 with fused recall 1.00 and 4/4 critical must-find. The root cause is not only the fixture: evaluate_retrieval_benchmark receives document rankings with no candidate provenance, channel, or backend identity, so it has no information with which to reject a lane whose result came from a channel other than the one the lane names. The per-lane scores recorded by O02-0002 therefore do not establish per-lane retrieval capability.

demonstrated: per-lane aggregation without averaging away a failing lane

checks.asserted_on: the acceptance gate assert_benchmark_thresholds, not the raw scores

checks.note: every canonical lane has a query, a labelled target present in the corpus, and at least one distractor
each fixture query uses a family the canonical plan binds to that lane

secondary_findings.observation: evaluate_retrieval_benchmark writes live_network_calls: 0 and live_llm_calls: 0 as literals into its own return value, and assert_benchmark_thresholds reads those literals back to decide whether the run was local and deterministic. Neither is an argument or a measurement.
secondary_findings.reproduced: the check refuses only a hand-edited report; no genuine benchmark run can make it fire
secondary_findings.not_claimed: no evidence the current benchmark makes network or model calls; the finding is that this check could not detect it if it did

secondary_findings.observation: seal_backend_request, seal_backend_response, validate_sealed_backend_request, validate_backend_response, and build_candidate_set all now take a required keyword-only query_plan, binding each backend call to the exact O01 QueryPlan. The O02 tests that exercise them were not updated: 37 call sites across tests/retrieval/test_o02_integrity_and_fallback.py and tests/retrieval/test_o02_non_vector_guard.py omit it.
secondary_findings.consequence: retrieval_integrity_and_fallback_test and non_vector_release_guard_test raise TypeError at their first contract call. Two of O02's six required checks cannot run at all, so neither currently demonstrates anything.
secondary_findings.reproduced: static signature comparison against the current contract module, confirmed by calling seal_backend_request(DATA['request']) exactly as the fixtures do and receiving TypeError: missing 1 required keyword-only argument: 'query_plan'
secondary_findings.origin: the query_plan binding was added to python/epistemic_foundry/retrieval/lanes/contracts.py in uncommitted work from an earlier session; the callers in O02's own test scope were left behind
secondary_findings.repair: each affected fixture now compiles the QueryPlan its request is a lane projection of, taking the forward queries from the fixture's own query batch, and binds plan_hash to that plan. The projected lexical query hash equals the hash the fixture already recorded, which is what confirms the plan matches the fixture rather than merely satisfying the signature. All 37 call sites now pass query_plan; a static re-audit reports 0 missing.
secondary_findings.post_repair_state: the five contract functions execute end to end against the fixture, and the previously unrunnable provenance audit now runs and passes
secondary_findings.not_claimed: no judgement on whether the query_plan binding itself is correct; it looks like a genuine tightening. The finding is that its callers were not carried with it.

changed_files.change: added fixture-integrity checks and an executable lexical-substitution negative control

spec_gaps: Changing the required-check semantics so that a benchmark truthfully reporting BLOCKED for unserved lanes counts as an O02 PASS is a shared acceptance change. It affects the acceptance authority and the development-manifest projection, and has no authorized owner or exact postimage. It is not made here.
not_verified: whether non_vector_release_guard_test carries the same construct-validity defect; the decisive audit is a provenance mutation, and it could not be run because that check's own call sites no longer match the contract signatures (see O02_REQUIRED_CHECK_CALLSITE_DRIFT)
whether a discriminating corpus is constructible without new retrieval capability

the attempt records the substitution run's index snapshot, index versions, backend and adapter identity, and observed candidate channels, but does not persist the full per-query ranking or per-candidate hashes; a replayer would rebuild the index from the recorded fixture hashes rather than replay stored candidate records

sibling_check_audits.audit: same-vocabulary reversal, entity rename, and ontology-mapping removal
sibling_check_audits.detail: classify_relation_direction answers all seven fixture cases correctly. Reversing only the argument order flips SAME_DIRECTION and REVERSE_DIRECTION in both directions, so the classifier reads the relation rather than the vocabulary. Renaming the entities leaves the verdict unchanged, so it does not depend on fixture-specific names. Removing the inverse-predicate mapping turns INVERSE_PREDICATE into UNRESOLVED rather than inventing the inverse.
sibling_check_audits.contrast_with_benchmark: this fixture already carries the contrastive pairs the benchmark lacks: SAME_DIRECTION and REVERSE_DIRECTION share identical tokens and differ only in argument order

sibling_check_audits.audit: provenance mutation: real non-vector origin, vector-only origin, and vector result relabelled as lexical
sibling_check_audits.detail: run after repairing the call-site drift. A genuine LEXICAL+CITATION_GRAPH candidate yields ceiling PASS with reason non_vector_origin_present. A SEMANTIC-only candidate yields PARTIAL with reason vector_only_release. Relabelling the semantic candidate as LEXICAL is refused as CANDIDATE_HASH_MISMATCH when the hash is left alone, and as CHANNEL_OBSERVATION_MISMATCH when the self-hash is recomputed, so the guard reconciles the claimed channel against the recorded backend observation rather than trusting the label.
sibling_check_audits.contrast_with_benchmark: this guard does exactly what the benchmark gate cannot: it has the provenance and it checks it

not_claimed: that any unserved lane was implemented
next: Two things, in order. First, the benchmark gate must receive candidate provenance: while evaluate_retrieval_benchmark scores bare document rankings, no fixture can make it reject channel substitution. Second, a corrected fixture requires a corpus larger than the cutoff, queries that do not carry unique document keys, per-lane contrastive hard negatives, and metamorphic pairs for the relation-sensitive lanes. Unserved lanes stay BLOCKED and unscored rather than being assigned zero or perfect metrics.
